formulations.label: Tablets

src.q: Each tablet contains 16 mg betahistine dihydrochloride equivalent to 10.42 mg betahistine.

items.t: Vertigo, tinnitus and hearing loss associated with Ménière's syndrome.

items.t: Not recommended under 18 years (insufficient safety and efficacy data).

items.t: Initially 16 mg three times daily, preferably with meals. Maintenance usually 24 to 48 mg daily.

src.q: initially 16mg three times daily taken preferably with meals. Maintenance doses are generally in the range 24-48 mg daily.

src.q: Hypersensitivity to the active substance or to any of the excipients.

items.t: History of peptic ulcer: caution.

src.q: Caution is advised in the treatment of patients with a history of peptic ulcer.

items.t: Bronchial asthma: intolerance seen in a few patients; monitor carefully.

src.q: Clinical intolerance to Serc in bronchial asthma patients has been shown in a relatively few patients. These patients need to be carefully monitored during the therapy.

items.t: MAO inhibitors (including MAO-B selective, e.g. selegiline) may inhibit betahistine metabolism: caution.

src.q: Caution is recommended when using betahistine and MAO inhibitors (including MAO-B selective) concomitantly.

items.t: Antihistamines: in theory each may reduce the effect of the other.

src.q: interaction of betahistine with antihistamines may in theory affect the efficacy of one of these drugs

items.t: No in-vivo interaction studies; no CYP450 inhibition expected.

src.q: No in-vivo interaction studies have been performed. Based on in-vitro data no in-vivo inhibition on Cytochrome P450 enzymes is expected.

items.t: No specific trials; post-marketing experience suggests no dose adjustment appears necessary.

src.q: There are no specific clinical trials available in this patient group, but according to post-marketing experience no dose adjustment appears to be necessary.

items.t: No adequate human data; animal studies do not show harm. As a precaution, it is preferable to avoid in pregnancy.

src.q: As a precautionary measure, it is preferable to avoid the use of betahistine during pregnancy.

items.t: Unknown whether it passes into human milk (it does in rats). Weigh the importance of the drug to the mother against the benefits of nursing and risks to the child.

src.q: It is not known whether betahistine is excreted in human milk.
The importance of the drug to the mother should be weighed against the benefits of nursing and the potential risks for the child.

items.t: Animal studies showed no effect on fertility in rats.

src.q: Animal studies did not show effects on fertility in rats.

items.t: Common: nausea, dyspepsia, headache. Mild gastric complaints can be helped by taking with meals or lowering the dose.
